author: reek
body: Bump-allocate `size` bytes aligned to `align` (a power of two) and zero them. The HBA reads these structures by DMA, so a stale byte is a real command; zeroing is not hygiene, it is correctness.

author: reek
body: Enable memory space (bit 1) and bus master (bit 2). Bus master is what lets the HBA write our buffer; without it the command completes and the buffer stays empty.

author: reek
body: A board can carry several SATA disks on one HBA; `ahci-find-nth` opens the n-th of them, counted in port order, so a caller choosing a MEDIUM (GopDisk's selection cells) can address each disk rather than whichever answers first.

author: reek
body: A port counts only when it is implemented, its PHY reports a device with communication established (SSTS.DET == 3), and its signature is a plain SATA disk (an ATAPI drive answers a different command set).

author: reek
body: Command header slot 0: five dwords of command FIS, one PRDT entry. Bit 6 of the first dword marks a write (host to device); a read leaves it clear.

author: reek
body: Wait for the command-issue bit to clear. A task-file error (IS.TFES) aborts the wait: the command failed and the buffer is meaningless.
